It is a very common question, and the short answer is no—Muslims do not worship the Kaaba!

Muslims worship God alone. When Muslims face the Kaaba The qiblah during their prayers Prayer or circle around it, they are not worshiping the structure itself. Instead, they are obeying God's command to face a unified direction. Just as placing your forehead on the ground during prayer is an act of worshiping God—not worshiping the earth itself—facing the Kaaba is an act of obedience to God.

The Kaaba is a physical building made of stone that cannot bring benefit or cause harm by itself. It serves as a historical symbol for the Oneness of God Tawhid / Oneness of God, built to worship God alone, and Muslims direct all their devotion, prayer, and worship strictly to God, not to any stone or creature.

مرحباً بك. سؤالك مهم، ولكن القرآن الكريم ليس من تأليف النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

﴿إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [الحاقة: 40]

. فلو كان من تأليفه أو من عند بشر، لما وجدنا فيه وجوهاً من الإعجاز التاريخي والتشريعي والبلاغي والعلمي التي عجز عنها أهل ذلك الزمان. علاوة على ذلك، كان الوحي يتأخر أحياناً عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فترات يحجم خلالها عن الإجابة حتى يعود إليه الوحي، فلو كان القرآن من تلقاء نفسه لما احتاج لانتظار الوحي في ردوده. كما أن القرآن يضم آيات فيها عتاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهو ما يؤكد أنه ليس من صناعة بشريّة، بل هو كلام الله المنزل عليه. يسعدني سماع رأيك أو أي سؤال إضافي تدور حوله فكرتك.

It is a very common question, and it is completely natural to wonder about it. The short answer is that Islam did not spread by the sword; rather, it spread through invitation and reasoned argument.

The teachings of Islam instruct Muslims to call people to God’s path with wisdom, goodly exhortation, and respectful discussion. If we look at history, we find that people embraced Islam by choice. Many early companions, including prominent figures and various groups, accepted Islam freely without compulsion, whether in Makkah, Madinah, or elsewhere. Even when territories came under Muslim rule, people were not forced to convert; many chose Islam after seeing the character, fairness, and values of the Muslims living among them.

If you have any other questions about this or anything else, feel free to ask.

It is natural to wonder why scholars sometimes reach different conclusions. These differences do not come from personal desires, but from objective scholarly reasons. For example, scholars might understand a text differently, some might have access to a specific Hadith (saying or action of the Prophet, peace be upon him) while others do not, or they may weigh types of evidence differently. Importantly, these differences are in practical branches of daily life rather than the core foundations of faith, and they reflect the honest efforts of qualified scholars studying the sources.

جزاك الله خيرًا على سؤالك. هذا السؤال يتعلق بحالتك الخاصة، والحكم فيه يحتاج إلى معرفة تفاصيل وضعك من عالِمٍ مؤهَّل، ولذلك لا نستطيع أن نعطيك حكمًا هنا. ننصحك بعرض سؤالك بتفاصيله على عالِمٍ أو جهة إفتاء موثوقة في بلدك، أو على مركز إسلامي قريب منك. ويسعدنا أن نجيبك عن أي سؤال عام عن الإسلام.
لم نجد في المصادر المعتمدة لدينا حديثًا صحيحًا يطابق ما ذكرت، ولا يصح أن نَنسب إلى النبي ﷺ كلامًا دون مصدر موثَّق. إن كان لديك نص الحديث أو مصدره فأرسله لنا لنتحقق منه.

Tawhid is an important Islamic concept that means the Oneness of God. It is the belief that Godhood, lordship, His names, and His attributes belong to God alone, rather than being shared with anything else. Please feel free to ask if you would like to know more about this!

In English, the word التوحيد is translated as Tawhid, or the Oneness of God. This means believing that lordship, Godhood, and God's names and attributes belong to God alone. Let me know if you would like to explore this further!

I understand why it might seem strict from the outside, but the ban on alcohol in Islam is actually meant to protect people and society from real harm.

One of the most important goals in Sharia / Islamic law and guidance is protecting the mind and intellect, which is what makes a person responsible for their actions. Alcohol weakens the mind, leading to foolish behavior, bad speech, and even enmity and hatred between people.

It also causes major financial harm by wasting money on something that brings no real benefit and can ruin families and lead to poverty. Beyond that, it distracts a person from Remembrance and Prayer, pulling them away from what truly matters spiritually.

Islam doesn't ban things simply to control people, but to protect our well-being, our relationships, and our minds. Would you like to chat more about how Islam views personal responsibility and care for the body?

Scholars hold different views on various matters, but regarding music and instruments, the majority of scholars consider them forbidden, relying on texts such as a statement reported in Sahih al-Bukhari. Because details and nuances can vary, it is best to consult a specialist for a more thorough understanding.

You are very close! The exact wording of that verse is

﴿قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ [الإخلاص: 1]
“Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم): "He is Allâh, (the) One.” (Quran 112:1)

, which means "He is Allah, the One."

This points to a central concept in Islam called Tawhid (the Oneness of God). Tawhid is the greatest and most fundamental truth in the Islamic worldview. It is the core message that all of God's messengers came with, calling people to recognize and worship God alone without any partners.

Would you like to explore more about what this means for daily life?

Not at all! When Muslims say "inshallah," which means "If Allâh wills"

﴿وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ﴾ [القلم: 18]
“Without saying: Inshâ’ Allâh (If Allâh wills).” (Quran 68:18)

, they aren't usually trying to politely say no. Instead, it is a way of acknowledging that everything happens by God's will and reminding ourselves that our future plans depend on Him. Your coworker likely intends to get the report done, while leaving the final outcome in God's hands. It reflects a mindset of humility about the future rather than a hidden refusal. مسلمان کعبہ کی عبادت ہرگز نہیں کرتے، بلکہ تمام عبادات جیسے کہ نماز صرف اللہ اکیلے کے لیے ہے جو ہمارا پیدا کرنے والا ہے۔ جب مسلمان نماز پڑھتے ہیں تو وہ کعبہ کی طرف رخ کرتے ہیں، اور یہ کعبہ کی عبادت نہیں ہوتی بلکہ یہ اللہ تعالیٰ کے حکم کی اطاعت ہے (

﴿قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِي السَّمَاءِ ۖ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضَاهَا ۚ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ ۚ وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنْتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ ۗ وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ ۗ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [البقرة: 144]
ہم آپ کے چہرے کو بار بار آسمان کی طرف اٹھتے ہوئے دیکھ رہے ہیں، اب ہم آپ کو اس قبلہ کی جانب متوجہ کریں گے جس سے آپ خوش ہوجائیں، آپ اپنا منھ مسجد حرام کی طرف پھیر لیں اور آپ جہاں کہیں ہوں اپنا منھ اسی طرف پھیرا کریں۔ اہل کتاب کو اس بات کے اللہ کی طرف سے برحق ہونے کا قطعی علم ہے اور اللہ تعالیٰ ان اعمال سے غافل نہیں جو یہ کرتے ہیں۔ (قرآن 2:144)

)۔ جیسے ہم زمین پر سجدہ کرتے ہیں تو زمین کی عبادت نہیں کرتے، بلکہ اللہ کے حکم پر سجدہ کرتے ہیں۔ اللہ تعالیٰ نے دنیا بھر کے مسلمانوں کو ایک ہی سمت یعنی کعبہ کی طرف رخ کرنے کا حکم دیا ہے تاکہ سب کی سمت ایک ہو جائے، کیونکہ کعبہ توحید (یعنی اللہ کو ایک ماننے) کی ایک تاریخی نشانی ہے جسے حضرت ابراہیم نے بنایا تھا۔ اگر کوئی شخص کعبہ کی عبادت کرے تو وہ اسلام کی بنیادی تعلیم یعنی توحید کے خلاف ورزی کرتا ہے۔ کیا آپ کے ذہن میں اس بارے میں کوئی اور سوال ہے؟

I understand why it might look that way from the outside, but Muslims do not worship the Ka'bah or any stone. The Ka'bah is a physical structure that cannot harm or benefit on its own, and anyone who intends to worship it would be going against the core of Islamic faith, which is Tawhid (Oneness of God). When Muslims face the Ka'bah during prayer Prayer, or when they touch or kiss the Black Stone, they are following God's command. Facing this direction unites Muslims worldwide in worshipping God alone, just as putting one's forehead on the ground in prayer is directed only to God, not to the earth itself. Worship in Islam belongs exclusively to God.

Muslims do not worship the KaꜤbah at all; worship is directed to God alone. When Muslims face the KaꜤbah during prayer, it is not because the structure itself is holy or powerful, but because God commanded them to face this specific direction. This unites Muslims around the world to face one unified point when they worship God, just as placing one's forehead on the ground in prayer is worshiping God, not the earth itself. The KaꜤbah is a historic building that serves as a symbol of the oneness of God, having been built as a house dedicated to God. Anyone who intentionally worships the KaꜤbah itself would be going against the core of Islamic faith, which requires directing all worship solely to God.

It is completely natural to wonder about where the Qur’an came from. But when you look closely at it, it doesn't fit the idea of something written by a human. For one thing, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, was known among his people as someone who never lied, so it doesn't make sense that he would suddenly claim something was from God if it wasn't.

Also, there were times when questions were asked and the Prophet had to wait for the revelation to come before he could answer, rather than just making something up on the spot. The Qur’an itself contains deep truths, historical accounts, and knowledge of the unseen that people at that time could not have simply produced on their own. It comes directly from God, as the text itself mentions

﴿إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [الحاقة: 40]
“That this is verily, the word of an honoured Messenger [i.e. Jibrîl (Gabriel) or Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم which he has brought from Allâh].” (Quran 69:40)

.

نہیں، قرآن حضرت محمد صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم کا اپنا لکھا ہوا یا خود کا کلام نہیں ہے، بلکہ یہ اللہ تعالیٰ کی طرف سے نازل کردہ کتاب ہے۔ اس بات کی کئی دلیلیں ہیں؛ جیسے کہ قرآن میں ایسی فصاحت، تاریخی، تشریعی اور علمی معجزات ہیں جو کوئی انسان اس زمانے میں پیش نہیں کر سکتا تھا۔ اس کے علاوہ، جب کبھی آپ صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم سے کوئی سوال کیا جاتا اور آپ کے پاس فوری جواب نہ ہوتا، تو آپ وحی یعنی اللہ کے حکم کا انتظار کرتے تھے، اور وحی آنے پر آپ کی جسمانی اور نفسیاتی حالت میں واضح تبدیلیاں بھی دیکھی جاتی تھیں جو بتاتی ہیں کہ یہ کسی انسان کا تخیل یا تصنیف نہیں ہے۔

سؤالك مهم جداً ومكرر، والحقيقة أن الإسلام لم ينتشر بالسيف، بل انتشر بالدعوة والحكمة والموعظة الحسنة.

فالكثير من الأمم والشعوب دخلت في الإسلام بمجرد الدعوة والتواصل مع المسلمين دون حروب، مثل المسلمين في الصين وجاوا وعدد من بلدان إفريقيا وغيرها من مناطق العالم التي وصلها الإسلام عن طريق التجار والدعاة. فالإسلام يخاطب العقول والقلوب بالحكمة، ولو احتجت لأي توضيح آخر يسعدني سؤالك.

It is completely understandable why hearing certain verses out of context can raise concerns, but Islam is fundamentally a religion of peace that places the highest value on human life.

The verses about fighting and Jihad were not meant to promote violence or indiscriminately shed blood; rather, they were prescribed as a means of self-defense to stop ongoing aggression, protect the vulnerable, and restore peace. Even when fighting was necessary, Islamic law established strict moral rules that completely prohibit harming non-combatants, such as women, children, and the elderly.

If you would like, we can look more closely at the context behind these verses so you can see how they were actually applied.

علماء کے فتوے مختلف ہونے کی بنیادی وجہ یہ ہے کہ وہ فروعی اور ذيلي مسئلوں میں دلائل کو سمجھنے اور اجتہاد کرنے میں الگ الگ رائے رکھتے ہیں، جبکہ دین کی بنیادی اور اصل باتیں سب کے نزدیک متفقہ ہیں۔ یہ اختلاف کسی ذاتی غرض کی وجہ سے نہیں ہوتا، بلکہ اس کے علمی اسباب ہوتے ہیں؛ مثلاً بعض اوقات کسی عالم تک کوئی خاص حدیث یا دلیل نہیں پہنچتی یا ان کا فہم متن سے الگ ہوتا ہے، یا پھر وہ استدلال کے لیے قياس یا کسی اور ضابطے کو استعمال کرتے ہیں۔ اگر اس بارے میں آپ کا کوئی اور سوال ہو تو ضرور پوچھیے۔

أهلاً بك! "التوحيد" هو أساس الإسلام، ومعناه ببساطة: إفراد الله تعالى بالربوبية والألوهية، ووصفه بكل ما وصف به نفسه أو جاء به الوحي من أسمائه الحسنى، بحيث لا نعبد أحداً سواه ولا نشرك معه أحداً، ولا يقتصر هذا المعنى على مجرد وحدانية العدد، بل هو إقرار تام لله بالوحدانية والكمال في صفاته وأفعاله واستحقاقه للعبادة وحده. هل تحب أن نوضح نقطة معينة أكثر؟

سلام! آپ کا یہ سوال بہت اچھا ہے۔ لفظ "توحید" کا مطلب یہ ہے کہ اللہ تعالی کو اکیلا اور یکتا ماننا؛ یعنی یہ عقیدہ رکھنا کہ اللہ ہی سب کا رب ہے، وہی اکیلا عبادت کے لائق ہے، اور اس کے پیارے نام اور صفات صرف اسی کے لیے خاص ہیں۔ اس کا مطلب صرف یہ نہیں کہ وہ گنتی میں ایک ہے، بلکہ اس کا مطلب یہ ہے کہ اس کی ربوبیت، الوہیت اور صفات میں کوئی اس کا شریک نہیں۔ اگر آپ اس کے بارے میں مزید کچھ پوچھنا چاہیں تو ضرور بتائیے گا۔

The correct English term for Sharia is "Sharia" or "Islamic law and guidance". It is definitely not just Islamic criminal law! In fact, Sharia refers to the total sum of rules and regulations that God has set for His servants and revealed to His Messenger, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It covers a wide range of areas, including detailed rulings on belief, worship, everyday transactions, and morality, rather than being limited to just legal punishments. It is completely understandable to wonder about rules like this, especially when something seems appealing. In Islam, God has given us guidance out of care for us, allowing what is good and wholesome and protecting us from what is harmful. When it comes to pork, it is mentioned in the Quran as something impure

﴿قُلْ لَا أَجِدُ فِي مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّمًا عَلَىٰ طَاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً أَوْ دَمًا مَسْفُوحًا أَوْ لَحْمَ خِنْزِيرٍ فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ أَوْ فِسْقًا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ ۚ فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغٍ وَلَا عَادٍ فَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [الأنعام: 145]
“Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم): "I find not in that which has been revealed to me anything forbidden to be eaten by one who wishes to eat it, unless it be Maitah (a dead animal) or blood poured forth (by slaughtering or the like), or the flesh of swine (pork); for that surely is impure or impious (unlawful) meat (of an animal) which is slaughtered as a sacrifice for others than Allâh (or has been slaughtered for idols, or on which Allâh’s Name has not been mentioned while slaughtering). But whosoever is forced by necessity without wilful disobedience, nor transgressing due limits; (for him) certainly, your Lord is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful."” (Quran 6:145)

, and keeping away from it safeguards health and physical well-being. Ultimately, God knows what benefits us and what harms us in both our faith and our daily lives. If you would like to explore more about how Islam views health and food, feel free to ask!

It is a great question to ask. In Islam, the core belief is Tawhid, which means the Oneness of God — believing that God is entirely one, without any partners, associates, or shares in His divinity and lordship.

Some people wonder if the Quran supports a plurality of gods or something like a Trinity because it sometimes uses plural pronouns like "We" or "Indeed, We" when speaking about God. However, in the Arabic language, these pronouns are often used by a single person of high status or authority for magnification and glorification, not to indicate multiple entities. Since sound proofs establish the absolute Oneness of God, understanding these expressions as a sign of majesty and greatness is the correct way, rather than interpreting them as polytheism or a Trinity.

Muslims believe that Jesus was not crucified

﴿وَقَوْلِهِمْ إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا الْمَسِيحَ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَٰكِنْ شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ ۚ وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ لَفِي شَكٍّ مِنْهُ ۚ مَا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلَّا اتِّبَاعَ الظَّنِّ ۚ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِينًا ۝١٥٧ بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ ۚ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا ۝١٥٨﴾ [النساء: 157-158]
“(157) And because of their saying (in boast), "We killed Messiah ‘Îsâ (Jesus), son of Maryam (Mary), the Messenger of Allâh," - but they killed him not, nor crucified him, but it appeared so to them [the resemblance of ‘Îsâ (Jesus) was put over another man (and they killed that man)], and those who differ therein are full of doubts. They have no (certain) knowledge, they follow nothing but conjecture. For surely; they killed him not [i.e. ‘Îsâ (Jesus), son of Maryam (Mary) عليهما السلام]: (158) But Allâh raised him [‘Îsâ (Jesus)] up (with his body and soul) unto Himself (and he عليه السلام is in the heavens). And Allâh is Ever All-Powerful, All-Wise.” (Quran 4:157-158)
